failures.message: sherpa_onnx.OfflineTts.generate() segfaults (native crash, exit code 139) using the sriram09764/itantra-tts-onnx community sherpa-onnx VITS export for Telugu, with sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 on Windows CPU. Model construction/loading succeeds; the crash is inside synthesis and is reproducible even with a single trivial Telugu word ('నమస్తే'), ruling out a text-length or punctuation issue. A separate community ONNX export of the same underlying facebook/mms-tts-tel checkpoint (willwade/mms-tts-multilingual-models-onnx) loads and synthesizes correctly via plain onnxruntime, so the failure is specific to this conversion or to sherpa-onnx's VITS runner expectations for it, not to the environment or the base model.

Both Vakyansh Telugu Glow-TTS voices require compiling the repo's monotonic_align Cython extension (src/glow_tts/monotonic_align, a setup.py build_ext step) before inference can run. At the time this was first recorded, no C compiler appeared to be on PATH and the system drive (C:) had only about 3GB free, too little to safely install Visual Studio Build Tools. RESOLVED 2026-09-13: Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with the C++ workload was already installed on this host, just not on PATH; located cl.exe directly via vswhere, ran vcvarsall.bat to capture the MSVC environment, and built monotonic_align successfully. Both voices now have published samples.

The male Vakyansh Telugu voice segfaults intermittently during synthesis of the primary sentence on this hardware (2 crashes out of 5 total attempts observed, exit code 139). The female voice, using the same code path and shared vocoder, never crashed across the same testing. Not root-caused: could be a numerical edge case specific to this checkpoint's weights (e.g. in the InvConvNear LU-based invertible convolution) or a Windows-specific native BLAS threading issue, since re-running the identical script with no code changes succeeds most of the time. Not blocking: the published sample is from a successful run, but this instability should be kept in mind before treating this voice as production-reliable.
